scenes.img: On snowy Mount Kailash, Shiva: blue-grey skin, matted hair piled up with a crescent moon, a snake around his neck, tiger-skin cloth, a trident, calm face and Parvati: gentle goddess in a red silk sari with gold jewellery and a gold crown sit together, with their two sons beside them: Ganesha: young god with an elephant head and one broken tusk, round belly, red dhoti, small gold crown, four arms; Kartikeya: handsome young warrior god, clean-shaven, gold crown, holding a spear, riding a great peacock.
scenes.text: On Mount Kailash lived Shiva and Parvati… and their two sons. Ganesha, with his elephant head. And his brother, Kartikeya.

scenes.img: The sage Narada (white beard, saffron robe, veena on his shoulder) holds out a single shining golden fruit to Shiva and Parvati on Mount Kailash, while both sons lean in eagerly.
scenes.text: One day the sage Narada came with a gift. A golden fruit of wisdom. But there was only one.

scenes.img: Shiva: blue-grey skin, matted hair piled up with a crescent moon, a snake around his neck, tiger-skin cloth, a trident, calm face raises a hand announcing a contest, Parvati: gentle goddess in a red silk sari with gold jewellery and a gold crown smiling beside him, as Ganesha: young god with an elephant head and one broken tusk, round belly, red dhoti, small gold crown, four arms and Kartikeya: handsome young warrior god, clean-shaven, gold crown, holding a spear, riding a great peacock listen.
scenes.text: Who should get it? Their parents said: whoever goes around the whole world three times… and comes back first.

scenes.img: Kartikeya: handsome young warrior god, clean-shaven, gold crown, holding a spear, riding a great peacock leaps onto his great peacock and shoots up into the sky from Mount Kailash, feathers flashing.
scenes.text: Kartikeya leapt onto his peacock and shot into the sky. He was the fastest of all the gods.

scenes.img: Ganesha: young god with an elephant head and one broken tusk, round belly, red dhoti, small gold crown, four arms looks down at his ride, a tiny mouse, sitting at his feet on Mount Kailash, as a peacock disappears into the far sky.
scenes.text: Ganesha looked at his ride. A tiny mouse. A big body, and a small mouse. He could never win that race.

scenes.img: Kartikeya: handsome young warrior god, clean-shaven, gold crown, holding a spear, riding a great peacock on his peacock flies fast over oceans, mountains, forests and deserts, the curve of the earth below.
scenes.text: Kartikeya flew over oceans, mountains, forests and deserts… faster, and faster.

scenes.img: Ganesha: young god with an elephant head and one broken tusk, round belly, red dhoti, small gold crown, four arms sits calmly on a rock on Mount Kailash, eyes half closed, thinking, his mouse beside him.
scenes.text: Ganesha sat quietly. He did not panic. He thought.

scenes.img: Ganesha: young god with an elephant head and one broken tusk, round belly, red dhoti, small gold crown, four arms walks with folded hands in a circle around his parents Shiva: blue-grey skin, matted hair piled up with a crescent moon, a snake around his neck, tiger-skin cloth, a trident, calm face and Parvati: gentle goddess in a red silk sari with gold jewellery and a gold crown, who sit together on Mount Kailash; faint footprints mark the circle around them.
scenes.text: Then he stood up, folded his hands… and slowly walked around his parents. Once. Twice. Three times.

scenes.img: Shiva: blue-grey skin, matted hair piled up with a crescent moon, a snake around his neck, tiger-skin cloth, a trident, calm face and Parvati: gentle goddess in a red silk sari with gold jewellery and a gold crown look at Ganesha: young god with an elephant head and one broken tusk, round belly, red dhoti, small gold crown, four arms with curious smiles, asking him something.
scenes.text: Why did you do that? they asked.

scenes.img: Ganesha: young god with an elephant head and one broken tusk, round belly, red dhoti, small gold crown, four arms stands before his parents Shiva: blue-grey skin, matted hair piled up with a crescent moon, a snake around his neck, tiger-skin cloth, a trident, calm face and Parvati: gentle goddess in a red silk sari with gold jewellery and a gold crown with folded hands, and behind the parents the whole earth, sun and stars are drawn faintly, as if they hold the world.
scenes.text: Ganesha said: you are my whole world. Everything I am comes from you. So I have gone around the world.

scenes.img: Parvati: gentle goddess in a red silk sari with gold jewellery and a gold crown places the shining golden fruit in the hands of Ganesha: young god with an elephant head and one broken tusk, round belly, red dhoti, small gold crown, four arms, while Shiva: blue-grey skin, matted hair piled up with a crescent moon, a snake around his neck, tiger-skin cloth, a trident, calm face smiles proudly.
scenes.text: Shiva and Parvati smiled… and gave him the fruit.

scenes.img: Kartikeya: handsome young warrior god, clean-shaven, gold crown, holding a spear, riding a great peacock lands on his peacock, tired and proud, and sees Ganesha: young god with an elephant head and one broken tusk, round belly, red dhoti, small gold crown, four arms already holding the golden fruit; his face falls, hurt and angry.
scenes.text: When Kartikeya came back, tired and proud… the fruit was already gone. He was hurt. And angry.

scenes.img: Kartikeya: handsome young warrior god, clean-shaven, gold crown, holding a spear, riding a great peacock sits alone on top of a green hill in the south, and Shiva: blue-grey skin, matted hair piled up with a crescent moon, a snake around his neck, tiger-skin cloth, a trident, calm face and Parvati: gentle goddess in a red silk sari with gold jewellery and a gold crown climb up the hill to comfort him.
scenes.text: The story goes that he went away to a hill in the south, Palani, to be alone. And his parents went to him there… because they loved him just as much.

scenes.img: Shiva: blue-grey skin, matted hair piled up with a crescent moon, a snake around his neck, tiger-skin cloth, a trident, calm face and Parvati: gentle goddess in a red silk sari with gold jewellery and a gold crown sit with both sons together again, Ganesha: young god with an elephant head and one broken tusk, round belly, red dhoti, small gold crown, four arms and Kartikeya: handsome young warrior god, clean-shaven, gold crown, holding a spear, riding a great peacock smiling at each other, the mouse and the peacock beside them.
scenes.text: Both sons were loved. One was fast. One was wise. Neither was less.

scenes.img: Close view of Ganesha: young god with an elephant head and one broken tusk, round belly, red dhoti, small gold crown, four arms smiling gently, holding the golden fruit, his mouse on his shoulder.
scenes.text: Ganesha did not win because he was faster. He won… because he saw what mattered most.
Krishna says in the Gita… Do your work steady in yourself. Be the same in success and in failure. That evenness… is called yoga.
